Nina Patel: Heads-up — I found a weird signal in the reranker holdout. Some docs include a small metadata header like `uploaded_by: crawler_xyz` and `last_updated: 2024-02-...` that seems to be leaking into relevance judgments.
Samir Gupta: ugh. do you have an example?
Nina Patel: yep — excerpt from a doc in internal-recs: `---\nuploaded_by: crawler_batch_17\nlast_updated: 2024-02-11T03:12:45Z\nsource: web-archive\n---\nThe product description...`
Maria Chen: That could create spurious lexical overlap with queries that mention time or source. Did you see this in the candidate sets or just reference docs?
Nina Patel: both. In a small sample where queries had "recent" or specific dates, reranker bumped docs with matching `last_updated` strings. NDCG@10 moved +0.02 for those queries vs baseline.
Ben O'Neill: +0.02 seems small but systematic. Is this affecting our holdout->prod gap?
Nina Patel: Possibly. When I removed metadata lines before scoring, the global NDCG@10 dropped by 0.013 (i.e., we lost the artificial inflation). MRR changed less but skewed for recency-sensitive slices.
Samir Gupta: can you paste the quick ablation command you ran?
Nina Patel: sure — ran eval-harness with a simple preproc: `sed -n '/^---$/,/^---$/!p'` then tokenized as usual. Command: `python eval.py --candidates candidates.jsonl --preproc redaction --metrics ndcg,mrr --slice recency`
Maria Chen: Nice. We should 1) detect these headers automatically, 2) add a redact option in the harness, 3) re-run the holdout split. Also add a dataset-level flag so this doesn't silently change other datasets.
Ben O'Neill: I worry about over-redaction though. Some datasets intentionally include structured fields (title, author) that might be legitimate signals. We need whitelist vs blacklist.
Samir Gupta: proposal: three-step experiment:
- A: no redaction (current baseline)
- B: redact YAML-like frontmatter (lines between `---` markers)
- C: redact any `\w+: \S+` lines at doc start up to first blank line (more aggressive)
Run A/B/C across three datasets: internal-recs, web-qa-aug, enterprise-kb. Compare NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR, plus per-slice recency and source-name mention.
Nina Patel: + add token-level overlap check: compute fraction of tokens in query that come from metadata region vs body. We saw some queries were 30% overlap with the header tokens for short queries.
Maria Chen: Can we get a quick script to flag candidate-docs with headers? infra-bot: we can run a grep job across the candidate store. Want me to kick it off?
Ben O'Neill: yes please. Also include counts by dataset and by time window so we know if this is modern crawl artifact.
infra-bot: kicked off grep job: pattern `^---$` -> scanning candidates bucket. ETA ~45m. I will post full counts when done.
Samir Gupta: after infra counts, let's schedule the ablation runs. Nina, can you add the three-preproc configs to the eval harness and produce a runbook with exact seeds and batching so results are reproducible?
Nina Patel: on it. I'll:
- add `preproc_mode: none|frontmatter|aggressive` to harness
- pin random seed and batch order
- run on dev-host with the same model and quantization settings as earlier experiments
I expect each dataset run to take ~2h.
Maria Chen: When we compare, make sure to include p-values or bootstrap CIs for NDCG delta. We should avoid chasing noise.
Ben O'Neill: Agreed. Also: if redaction reduces our measured NDCG significantly but it's actually removing a legitimate signal for product search, we need to communicate to product teams. Keep provenance notes.
Nina Patel: noted. I'll attach per-query examples for top-delta queries so reviewer can eyeball. Also will include a small script to compute token-origin overlap.
Samir Gupta: one more thought — could tokenization differences make header tokens more or less impactful after quantized model changes? Probably minor but include quantized and fp16 runs if cheap.
Nina Patel: good call. I'll do float32 + int8 quick check on a small shard.
eval-bot: FYI — last time we had unseen metadata leaks it caused a 0.025 NDCG@10 overestimate on mini-holdout in 2023-09. Recommended to run full-holdout ablation.
Nina Patel: thanks, eval-bot. I'll post results in this thread when infra finishes and the runs complete.
Maria Chen: 👍 Thanks Nina — this looks like a sensible plan.
Ben O'Neill: thanks all. If infra results show it's widespread we should add 'frontmatter redaction' as a default opt-in in the next eval harness patch release.
Nina Patel: agreed. Posting interim notes to the rerank docs repo too.
